blocks.text: The pages that should have carried the rest of the record fell everywhere — so the whole world is a hunting ground. Every map belongs to a **biome**, with its own look, its own ground and creatures of its own.

items: **Grassland** — open meadows with a few trees and plenty of flowers: the gentle starting country around Lastline. Most of its creatures are Neutral.
**Forest** — fallen leaves, ferns and mushrooms under the trees. Mostly Earth.
**Highland** — a near-treeless moor of short turf and boulders. Mostly Earth.
**Peaks** — above the treeline: bare gravel, snow and boulders. Mostly Wind.
**Snow** — a snowy pine forest, its ground always white. Mostly Water.
**Steppe** — golden tussocks with sun-baked ground between them. Mostly Wind.
**Coast** — sand, wet sand and shore pebbles, scattered with rocks. Mostly Water.
**Desert** — open orange dunes with a few stones. Mostly Fire.
**Volcanic** — black ash, glowing lava cracks and boulder fields. Mostly Fire.
**Swamp** — reedy marsh and mud under willows, water always standing in its hollows. Mostly Poison.
**Sacred** — an open birch meadow in flower, high among the clouds. Mostly Holy.
**Haunted** — withered grass, grave dirt and old dark cobbles among dead stumps. Mostly Undead.
**Mist** — pale moss and grey silt under willows, always in fog. Mostly Ghost.
**Corrupted** — where the blankness runs deepest; the most twisted pages gather here, on withered violet grass and purple-black soil. Mostly Dark.

blocks.text: A biome decides which element **most** of its creatures carry — a majority, never a rule: a snow field is mostly Water, but some of its creatures are Earth, Dark or Wind. Every map names the creatures that live on it.
The fields are not flat. Their ground rises and falls in **broad levels joined by slopes**, so there is always higher ground to climb and lower ground to look down on.

Some roads run through a **pass between rock cliffs**. You cannot climb a cliff face — but here and there a cliff runs out and its high ground **slopes down to meet the road**, and there you can walk up onto the top.
Monsters walk exactly the ground you walk: any slope you can climb, they can climb after you, and a cliff that stops you stops them too.

text: *Status: all fourteen biomes are in the game, and the world's maps are built and joined to one another by doors. Some biomes are still waiting for props of their own — palm trees, cacti, dead trees, reeds — and the towns for their buildings.*
